scope: FWD with training checkpoints, Qwen35B H2048 I512 E256 top8, 8192 nominal tokens/rank, EP2 L20X; final sample of each 5-warmup/20-sample run; seeds 123/124/125
notes: MainEnter is sampled by math thread 0 after programmatic_launch::wait, before local kernel initialization. No cross-GPU timestamps are subtracted.
MmaBegin means first operand stage is ready, immediately before entering MMA setup; not a hardware instruction issue timestamp.
First GEMM is relative to its own CTA MainEnter. Mean GEMM start averages all task MmaBegin offsets within a CTA. Mean start gap averages consecutive GEMM starts.

Ready wait is TileStart to MmaBegin. Math is MmaBegin to MathEnd, including subsequent staging waits, FP32 promotion and any X column-cache work. Epilogue is MathEnd to TileEnd including publication and synchronization.
The statistics aggregate per-CTA means, weighting every active CTA equally. FP8 and BF16 have different task schedules; matching CTA IDs do not mean matching task identities.
Both variants execute the same diagnostic binary. Timeline overhead can alter scheduling and elapsed times; do not treat these as production latency.
All traces have zero overflow, matching complete task boundaries; workload hashes match between FP8/BF16 at each seed.
For each seed, only the final measured sample is traced to disk. There are 3 seeds x 2 ranks x 132 CTAs = 792 CTA observations per dtype, not 792 distinct physical CTAs.

Matched-first-task cohort matches seed, rank, CTA and the actual first task identity (FC kind, M block, N column); 208 observations. It reduces first-task scheduling confounding but does not isolate quantization alone.
